children: Arabica coffee futures on the ICE exchange hit fresh five-week lows on Thursday on favourable weather and upbeat supply prospects, while raw sugar slid from 16-month peaks hit in the prior session.
COFFEE
* Arabica coffee
settled down 2.75 cents, or 0.9%, at $2.9535 per lb after hitting a fresh five-week low of $2.8975.

* A pick-up in exports from top grower Brazil is helping ease short-term supply tightness, while the return of rains bodes well for the flowering stage that will define next year's crop, dealers said.

* "Warehouses (in Brazil) are filling up and exports are picking up pace, casting aside worries over low certified stocks (at ICE exchange) to cover immediate delivery needs," said soft commodities analyst Judy Ganes.
* Brazil's 2026/27 coffee crop is seen at a record 77.2 million bags thanks to favourable weather, StoneX said, raising its outlook 2.6% from its March estimate.
* Robusta coffee
fell 0.9% to $3,374 a metric ton, after hitting a 2-1/2-month low of $3,329.
SUGAR
* Raw sugar
​​​settled down 0.63 cent, or 3.4%, at 18.07 cents per lb after hitting its highest since April 2025 at 18.77 on Wednesday.
* "There is no fundamental reason for the drop. The pullback look(s) to be more a consolidation move," said soft commodities analyst and consultant Michael McDougall.
* Sugar prices are being driven by widespread expectations of a looming deficit, with the International Sugar Organization forecasting a 300,000-ton shortfall in the 2026/27 season.
* Sugar production in Brazil's center-south fell 7.9% year on year in early August, the government said.
* White sugar
fell 2.3% to $526.60 a ton.
COCOA
* London cocoa
settled down £65, or 1.4%, to £4,514  per ton. The market hit a one-year high of £4,988 on Tuesday.
* Cocoa output in No. 2 grower Ghana is forecast to drop 18% to 38% in 2026/27 due to ageing trees, disease and failing pollination, the state-run cocoa marketer said.
* The El Nino weather pattern is also a concern for cocoa.
* Against that, however, ample global cocoa stockpiles should help cushion any hit to production from adverse weather, a Mondelez International executive said.
* The cocoa market still expects a surplus in 2026/27, albeit a narrow one.
* New York cocoa
lost 1.6% to $6,174 a ton.
